title: Relationship between chlorine decay and temperature in the drinking water
author: García-Ávila, Sánchez-Alvarracín, et al.

steps.title: Plan sampling schedule
steps.instruction: Collect a total of 30 water samples, taking one sample each month for six months (30 samples total) from the predetermined 30 sampling points across the six zones of the distribution network.

steps.title: Prepare sampling bottles
steps.instruction: Wash each 1000 mL plastic sampling bottle with a concentrated calcium hypochlorite solution adjusted to 10 mg L⁻¹, let the bottles stand for 24 h, rinse thoroughly with distilled water, and allow them to air‑dry before use, following the Ecuadorian standard and referenced studies.

steps.title: Collect water samples
steps.instruction: At each tap (household, commercial, educational, market, or distribution tank), run the water for approximately two minutes, then fill a prepared 1000 mL bottle according to INEN 2176, and place the bottle in a cooler to maintain a constant temperature during transport.

steps.title: Measure initial chlorine, pH, temperature
steps.instruction: Immediately after collection, take a 10 mL aliquot of the sample, add DPD reagent (N,N‑diethyl‑p‑phenylenediamine) as specified for the HACH DR 890 colorimeter, and record the free chlorine concentration; simultaneously measure pH and temperature with a HACH HQ40d multiparametric meter. Perform each measurement in duplicate.

steps.title: Incubate and monitor chlorine decay
steps.instruction: Store the remaining sample in an incubator, then transfer it to the laboratory and measure residual free chlorine every hour using the same DPD‑colorimetric method until the concentration approaches zero, recording each value for kinetic analysis.
